item.text:
**5B.1 Verdict**
- **Mostly yes, with important caveats.** Sharif’s 2024 economic agenda was framed around stabilization, tax-base broadening, SOE privatization/reform, tariff rationalization, and private-led growth. The main downside is that reforms were incomplete, the economy still relied on subsidies and protected sectors, and there were some investor-friendly concessions that can look like short-term appeasement.

**Evidence**
- **Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-07-12 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff)  
  The IMF says the authorities were pursuing a multi-year reform program to broaden the tax base, remove exemptions, improve SOE management, strengthen competition, protect vulnerable groups through BISP, and phase out distortionary incentives. That is strong evidence of an attempt to build durable, broader-based prosperity rather than rely on patronage.  
  IDs: `5B.1`

- **IMF Executive Board Concludes 2024 Article IV Consultation for Pakistan and Approves 37-month Extended Arrangement** | IMF | 2024-09-27 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr)  
  The IMF says Pakistan had taken key steps to restore stability under the prior SBA and that the new program aimed to entrench macro stability, broaden the tax base, strengthen competition, reform SOEs, improve public services, and build climate resilience. That is direct pro-sustainability evidence.  
  IDs: `5B.1`

- **Pakistan PM unveils broader plan to sell most state-owned firms** | Reuters | 2024-05-14 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-unveils-broader-plan-to-sell-most-state-owned-firms/2084587/)  
  Sharif said all state-owned enterprises would be privatized except strategic entities, explicitly framing the move as saving taxpayers’ money and repairing shaky public finances. That is a concrete action consistent with reducing rent channels and state patronage.  
  IDs: `5B.1`

- **PM says 5 IPPs to revisit contracts as Hub Power’s govt deal ends prematurely** | Reuters / Dawn | 2024-10-10 | [URL](https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298)  
  The government renegotiated power-purchase contracts to cut electricity tariffs and save about Rs60 billion a year, describing the move as in the “greater national interest.” This points to cost reduction and structural repair rather than short-term popularity alone.  
  IDs: `5B.1`

- **Pakistan: Second and Final Review Under the Stand-by Arrangement** | IMF | 2024-05-10 / 2024-04-29 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/10/pakistan-second-and-final-review-under-the-stand-by-arrangement-press-release-staff-report-548741)  
  The IMF says sustainable recovery required strict fiscal targets, a market-determined exchange rate, better tax collection, SOE reform, governance and anti-corruption reforms, and continued protection for the vulnerable through BISP. This supports a prosperity-building reading, but also shows how much structural repair remained unfinished.  
  IDs: `5B.1`

- **PAKISTAN: Reform Implementation Remains Critical for Continued Economic Recovery and Poverty Reduction, says World Bank** | World Bank | 2024-10-10 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank)  
  The World Bank says growth recovered to 2.5 percent, but poverty still rose and the government still needed to reform inefficient spending, untargeted subsidies, the tax system, trade and investment barriers, and the large state presence in the economy. This is supportive on intent, but it underscores that broad-based gains were not yet secured.  
  IDs: `5B.1`

- **Pakistan: 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-10-10 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152)  
  The IMF says Pakistan still had a narrow tax base, weak governance, an outsized state role, insufficient health and education spending, and a business environment that hindered investment. It also notes the program’s reliance on broadening taxes, reducing subsidies, and improving public investment management. That is the strongest evidence that the inherited economy still contained rent-seeking structures and that Sharif’s reforms were only partially displacing them.  
  IDs: `5B.1`

**Search gap**
- I did not find a 2024 source showing Sharif personally engaging in clear rent extraction or explicit loyalty-buying in the economic record.
- The best negative evidence is structural: Pakistan still depended on privileged sectors, subsidies, and a large state footprint, and some measures favored investor confidence or preserved short-term stability over deeper redistribution.
- So the record supports a reform-oriented intent, but not yet a fully transformed or fully broad-based prosperity outcome.
